title: Why he never arranged When the Saints Go Marching In
summary: Armstrong asked for a Saints arrangement, but Randolph avoided it as a religious song until he heard it from a sound truck after he had left.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: Well, who selected the songs to arrange? Did Louie say, you know, make me an arrangement on whatever?

Yes, Louie would, Louie would tell me. He'd tell me to make arrangements. There's one song he asked me to make an arrangement on and I never did make an arrangement on it. I kept on putting him off and (unintelligible) in the bag. I got it -- it's in the bag.
That was 'When the Saints Go Marching In.' I just didn't feel like -- I felt like there was other tunes that I could jazz other than just -- you know, I got a feeling about those things.
You had an objection about doing a religious song in a jazz band?

Yeah, I just didn't want -- I mean, I just didn't want to sit down and just be doing this. And finally one day after -- this is after I had left Louie, I'm sitting down in the front room -- I was extracting an arrangement and I heard that Eddie Pick -- Eddie is a fellow that used a sound and he advertised Pekin Cleaners and all the different things with the sound truck and I heard, 'Now, when the saints go,' and I said, 'Well, at last he got somebody,' (laughter)
